aiUseDisclosure: Codex authored the accepted innate-power victim stories, optional one-fight vows and two-exchange branches; the anonymous visitors are Morrow's past lives retained by the crown.

kitten.sacrifice: Gave away body heat to children during the old king's winter levy.
kitten.entrance: A small body crawls from the gutter and warms a dead lantern between its paws.

first.question: He took our coal for his palace. I kept the little ones warm until my paws went cold. Your windows are still lit.
choices: Take half my guard. Let my strikes carry 15% more force.
I will face you with the strength I have.
responses: For this fight, then. Half your guard; your strikes carry 15% more force. Please make it mean something.
He kept everything, too. I hoped you would be different.

kitten.remembered: The smallest one slept against my chest. I could not feel her breathing through the frost.

second.question: You can still open the doors. Why does it take a blade to make you listen?
choices: I let the years make the choices for me.
I cannot undo what he did.
responses: Then stop letting another winter choose who dies.
You can stop doing it again. That would be a start.

second.question: I am frightened. I came anyway. Will you?
choices: I will stand and hear you.
Go home. There is nothing for you here.
responses: Then do not hide behind that chair.
There was nothing there either. That is why I came.

alley.sacrifice: Suffocated while hiding children from crown raids rather than reveal their shelter.
alley.entrance: The lamps gutter in order; a sharp inhale reveals a body in the last shadow.

first.question: I held my breath under the floor while his soldiers counted the children. You stopped counting years ago.
choices: Half my guard for 15% stronger strikes. I will pay this time.
I will not bargain with another life.
responses: Only your guard. Only this fight. Your blows gain 15%; no child pays for it.
Another life? You say it like you cannot hear the boards beneath us.

alley.remembered: One child started to cough. I covered my own mouth so they would hear only me.

second.question: The houses below your walls are empty. Did you ever ask where everyone went?
choices: I thought silence meant they were safe.
I was keeping the kingdom alive.
responses: That is what he called it when the boots stopped.
A kingdom is not the stone that outlasts its people.

second.question: Look at me when you say you will not bargain.
choices: I should have opened the gates.
I have enemies beyond these walls.
responses: You knew where the hinges were. You stayed seated.
You learned his excuse more carefully than his name.

sailor.sacrifice: Drowned carrying refugees after the old king barred the flood gates.
sailor.entrance: Water gathers into bent silhouettes before a burdened body rises between them.

first.question: The flood came to the gate. He ordered it barred. I carried three across before the fourth pulled me under.
choices: Let half my guard sink. Give my strikes 15% more force.
I will carry my own strength into this.
responses: This burden is yours: half your guard, 15% more force, until our fight ends.
Then carry it. Do not put another body beneath it.

sailor.remembered: I kept one hand above the water long after I could no longer see the bank.

second.question: Your gates rust shut now. Do you call that mercy because you never gave the order?
choices: Neglect can kill as surely as an order.
I could not be everywhere.
responses: Then look at the weight before you strike it.
The gate was one place. You were on the other side.

second.question: Do you know what the drowned weigh?
choices: More than anyone should carry.
Enough. Put the dead down.
responses: The living become heavier when a king looks away.
I tried. They kept reaching for the shore.

acrobat.sacrifice: Broke its own body catching laborers from neglected palace scaffolds.
acrobat.entrance: A body hangs in an unfinished fall, then strikes the stone and stands unevenly.

first.question: The scaffold rope snapped. His steward charged us for it. I caught who I could with the bones I had left.
choices: Half my guard for 15% more striking force. I accept the fall.
I will not promise what I cannot bear.
responses: For this fight, your guard is halved and your strikes gain 15%. Land on your own bones.
You promised them safety by wearing the crown.

acrobat.remembered: The rope burned through my paw. I held on until the next body fell.

second.question: The west tower is falling now. You hear it from the throne, don't you?
choices: I kept mistaking it for thunder.
I was waiting for the right time.
responses: Then you have heard enough storms to know better.
So were the ones under it.

second.question: I cannot catch everyone this time.
choices: You should never have had to.
Then step aside and let me do my duty.
responses: Neither should they have had to jump.
Your duty has had centuries. I have one more fall.

witch.sacrifice: Took neighbors' deaths into her own body when royal medicine was withheld; calls those graves into a protector.
witch.entrance: Grave lights rise from scars; a death-knight kneels behind the small calling body.

first.question: He kept medicine for the court. They came to my door with their dying. I took each death inside me. They still answer.
choices: Take half my guard; let my strikes gain 15% force. No one else pays.
I will not take strength from those graves.
responses: Only you pay. Half your guard, 15% more force, for this fight. My dead remain mine.
You already live on what the crown took. Refusing to look is not refusal.

witch.remembered: The last neighbor asked whether it would hurt. I told her it would be over soon.

second.question: The one behind me held her daughter through the fever. Can your crown remember her name?
choices: It should not take a crown to remember her.
You brought an army to my door.
responses: Then remember without one.
No. I brought the people who never reached yours.

second.question: The grave-knight rises because I cannot carry them standing alone.
choices: I see what it costs you.
Dismiss it. We can speak without the dead.
responses: Then do not make me carry another king.
They were quiet while they lived. You do not get that silence twice.

knight.sacrifice: Turned executioners from a refuge gate; inherited bloodline marks spend the body to brace and accelerate it.
knight.entrance: A shoulder forces the doors apart as old bloodline tattoos kindle through cracked skin.

first.question: His executioners came for the gatekeepers. I braced the gate until the marks split my skin. Your seals are on it now.
choices: Half my guard for 15% stronger strikes. Open my protection instead.
I will not spend my body for a promise.
responses: Half your guard and 15% more force, this fight only. A promise ought to leave a mark.
You have spent other bodies without touching your own.

knight.remembered: The wood gave before my knees did. I could still hear them pushing from the other side.

second.question: These marks belonged to every guard before me. They burn faster when I run. What have you inherited?
choices: His throne. More of his silence than I meant to.
A kingdom that needs defending.
responses: Then break something he left you.
From whom? The hungry at the gate?

second.question: You call it peace when no one has strength left to knock.
choices: I will not call it peace again.
I have held this place together.
responses: Words are easy while your skin is whole.
So did the gate. Until we were crushed behind it.

thief.sacrifice: Erased its own place in the census to steal ration records for households the old king denied.
thief.entrance: Footprints cross empty moonlight; a body appears where their shadow should have been.

first.question: He erased a street from the ration book. I stole its pages back. By morning my own name was gone.
choices: Erase half my guard. Give my strikes 15% more force.
I will keep what is mine for this fight.
responses: Your guard is halved; your strikes gain 15%, until this fight ends. Nothing else is erased.
That is always where the crown begins.

thief.remembered: I left the pages on their doors. I could not remember which door had been mine.

second.question: You stopped keeping a census. Do people cease to hunger when you stop writing them down?
choices: I let them vanish because it was easier.
I did not know who was still there.
responses: At least let me be visible when you kill me.
That is what he wanted the book to say.

second.question: Look at my shadow. It knows where I stand even when you do not.
choices: I see you.
Come out where I can fight you.
responses: Keep looking when the blade comes.
You keep asking people to become easy to hurt.

quiet.sacrifice: Surrendered its voice to stop the execution bell; speaks here only through a remembered whisper.
quiet.entrance: The bell cuts out; a scarred paw rests at a throat that cannot make a sound.

first.question: The bell called them out. I gave my voice to stop it. In the silence, another name was read.
choices: Half my guard. Fifteen percent more force. Let this oath be mine.
I will listen without an oath.
responses: Half your guard; 15% more force. Only until this fight ends. Not another voice.
Then listen past the quiet.

quiet.remembered: My mouth kept moving. The bell kept swinging. Neither of us made a sound.

second.question: Your empty hall is quiet, too.
choices: I thought it meant I had hurt no one.
Tell me what you want.
responses: It meant there was no one left to hear.
An end to the bell. An end to the crown.

second.question: I cannot say it twice.
choices: You will not have to.
I am still here.
responses: Then hear it once.
So was he. Long after every plea was spent.

patchwork.sacrifice: Kept the erased victims' names in its own scarred body and now carries the trapped lives toward release.
patchwork.entrance: Walks in without charging; nine scars light in the order of the memories held by the crown.

first.question: Nine scars. Nine deaths the crown would not release. You have been fighting what it kept of you.
choices: Half my guard for 15% more force. This last debt is mine.
No more bargains. Tell me my name.
responses: Morrow. Half your guard; 15% more force, for this last fight. Even now you make yourself the price.
Morrow. Before the crown, before the names were taken, you were Morrow.

patchwork.remembered: You carried their names when the old king burned the records. The crown kept every life that tried to save them.

second.question: He made a prison of the crown. You made a kingdom of the waiting. They died under both.
choices: Then bring them home. Even if it ends me.
I can still rule differently.
responses: I did not come to forgive you. I came to open it.
They waited centuries for that answer. They will not wait again.

second.question: We were the child, the drowned, the one beneath the floor. We died trying to save them. What did you save?
choices: A chair. A silence. I know that now.
I will not let you take what is left.
responses: Then stand up, Morrow. Let the kingdom outlive you.
That is what he said when you came for his heart.
